title: Specified isomorphisms of finitely presented modules descend to a later stage
statement: Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed set, $(Z_i)_{i\in I}$ an inverse system of quasi-compact schemes [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] that are quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], with affine transition morphisms $q_{ji}:Z_j\to Z_i$ for $j\geq i$ [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Let $Z=\varprojlim_i Z_i$ with projections $q_i:Z\to Z_i$ be its limit in the category of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Here being a limit means $q_{ji}\circ q_j=q_i$ for $j\geq i$, and for every scheme $T$ and family $t_i:T\to Z_i$ satisfying $q_{ji}\circ t_j=t_i$ there is a unique morphism $t:T\to Z$ with $q_i\circ t=t_i$ for every $i$. For a sheaf of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], finite presentation means that every point has an open neighbourhood $U$ on which there is an exact sequence $\mathcal O_U^m\to\mathcal O_U^n\to F|_U\to0$ for finite $m,n$. All pullbacks are tensor pullbacks [def-pc-module-pullback], with iterated pullbacks identified by their canonical composition isomorphisms. Fix $i\in I$, finitely presented $\mathcal O_{Z_i}$-modules $F_i,G_i$, and an isomorphism $\phi:q_i^*F_i\xrightarrow{\sim}q_i^*G_i$. There exist $k\geq i$ and morphisms $$u_k:q_{ki}^*F_i\to q_{ki}^*G_i,\qquad v_k:q_{ki}^*G_i\to q_{ki}^*F_i$$ such that $$v_k\circ u_k=1_{q_{ki}^*F_i},\qquad u_k\circ v_k=1_{q_{ki}^*G_i},\qquad q_k^*u_k=\phi,\qquad q_k^*v_k=\phi^{-1}.$$ The last two equations use the canonical identifications $q_k^*q_{ki}^*F_i\cong q_i^*F_i$ and $q_k^*q_{ki}^*G_i\cong q_i^*G_i$. Thus $u_k$ is an isomorphism lifting the specified $\phi$, including its inverse, between the pullbacks of the fixed finite-stage models.

proof.text: Apply clause (2) of [lem-trf-fp-modules-affine-limit-descent] first to $\phi$, obtaining $a\ge i$ and $u_a:q_{ai}^*F_i\to q_{ai}^*G_i$, and then to $\phi^{-1}$, obtaining $b\ge i$ and $v_b:q_{bi}^*G_i\to q_{bi}^*F_i$. Their limit pullbacks are the specified maps, rather than merely some isomorphisms between the same objects. The cited node has exactly the given qcqs and affine-transition hypotheses.

proof.text: Choose j above a and b by directedness. Define refineMap by pulling each map to j and conjugating with the canonical composition comparisons. To identify the section-normalized comparisons in the statement with those of [lem-pc-tensor-pullback-composition-associativity], first use uniqueness of the normalized adjunction of [def-pc-module-pullback] to identify it with the adjunction chosen by the existing tensor-pullback theorem. The unit formula for adjoint uniqueness then identifies the two comparisons, including the equality transport along the cone equation. Apply the cited associativity identity and naturality of the composition comparisons: refineMap preserves the specified conjugated limit pullback. Thus the two maps f and g at j pull back to phi and its inverse. After conjugating their composites, the inverse identities of phi show that their limit pullbacks are identities.

proof.text: Use finite presentation from Step 1 and clause (3) of [lem-trf-fp-modules-affine-limit-descent] at j for f composed with g versus the identity of F_j, and for g composed with f versus the identity of G_j. Obtain a_prime and b_prime above j, then choose k above both. Naturality of the canonical finite-stage composition comparisons shows that equality persists from a_prime or b_prime to k. Pull f and g to k and conjugate with the finite-stage comparison to the direct pullbacks of the original models at i. Functoriality and cancellation of the comparison isomorphisms give both inverse identities. The specified limit pullback equations persist by the associativity and naturality calculation of Step 3. These are exactly the four required equations.
